topic: Smart Beta, Quant Funds and other Non-Traditional Index Funds
source_evidence: The custom-built indexes for these funds often use “factors” to select the fund’s investments. A factor is a characteristic or feature that is believed to cause certain types of securities to outperform or underperform the market as a whole. Examples of common factors are value, dividends or quality.
answer: Smart beta funds use custom-built indexes that select investments using one or more factors. A factor is a characteristic believed to influence whether certain securities outperform or underperform the market. Examples include value, dividends, and quality. These funds still track an index rather than having an adviser independently choose investments, so they are considered passively managed. Their use of a factor does not guarantee that they will outperform the market.
